messages:
Alex W: Quick sync — Product is pushing for the feature rollout next week but SRE flagged increased deploy toil + SLO risk. Need a lightweight sequencing playbook so we don't keep flipping between ship and stabilize.
Maria P: TL;DR of the ask from product?
Alex W: They want feature-flagged rollout to 20% users, full launch in 2 weeks. Engineering estimates ~2 dev-weeks; infra work to reduce toil ~1.5 dev-weeks, but could be parallel.
Samir: Concern: if we ship without improving caching and autoscale rules, p95 will jump and we'll burn onpager rotations. We should quantify risk vs value.
Elaine: From PM side — impact is real: a top-10 customer requested this and it materially affects renewal. We need a prioritization rule that balances account risk + SRE effort.
Jonah K: Proposal: use a modified RICE that includes SLO-risk as a negative modifier. RICE = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort; then subtract SLO_Risk_Score. Keep numbers coarse (1-10).
Maria P: Sounds reasonable. Can we do a quick scoring for the two options: A) ship fast with limited infra changes; B) delay 3 weeks to do automation + cache work?
Samir: I'll sketch scores. Option A: Reach=6, Impact=8, Confidence=7, Effort=3 => RICE=(6*8*7)/3=112. SLO_Risk=6 => Adjusted=106. Option B: Reach=6, Impact=8, Confidence=9, Effort=6 => RICE=(6*8*9)/6=72. SLO_Risk=2 => Adjusted=70. So pure RICE favors A but adjusted scores closer.
Elaine: So product still prefers A because customer renewal timeline. Can we do A + mitigations? e.g., temporary rate-limit + canary and kill-switch?
Jonah K: Yes — run a canary to 2% for 48 hours, increase to 20% with autoscaling policy in conservative mode. Add prefix KV cache TTL bump and shadow traffic to measure. That reduces SLO_Risk estimated to 3.
Alex W: That sounds like a middle path. We should define launch criteria checklist. Minimal launch criteria (must pass all):
```
- Canary at 2% for 48h with p95 < 2x baseline
- Auto-scaler headroom metrics green (CPU/GPU queued < 60%)
- Kill-switch documented with runbook and pager owners
- Post-launch regression smoke test (end-to-end) passing
- Nightly job created to backfill cache if miss rate spikes
```
Maria P: Good checklist. We should also attach clear ownership and rollback plan. Who owns the kill-switch?
Samir: SRE on-call (Jonah) owns immediate kill-switch. Engineering owns the long-term rollback/change. I'll create a short runbook snippet.
Jonah K: I'll own the canary orchestration and autoscaler policy. ACTION: Jonah to implement canary + conservative autoscaler by tomorrow EOD.
Elaine: ACTION: Elaine to confirm customer will accept staged rollout and update sales enablement.
Alex W: ACTION: Samir to write the runbook + document SLO measurement dashboard; include quick links to graphs.
Alex W: Also let's add an explicit toil-burn task to next sprint so we don't accrue more debt: tabled item "infra: reduce deploy steps" estimated 6 dev-days.
Maria P: Recap: we agreed on intermediate path (A + mitigations). If canary metrics show SLO regress > threshold, immediate rollback. We'll re-evaluate after 72h at 20%.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: feature-flag rollout -> canary (2%) by @Jonah K. Status: awaiting manual approval.
Jonah K: Manual approval granted, starting canary orchestration now. Will post status updates here. :rocket:
Alex W: Thanks all. If anyone sees unexpected alerts, @Jonah K is primary, @Samir backup. We'll reconvene in 24h for metrics readout.
Maria P: Filed follow-up RFC with scoring and checklist: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/infra-launch-playbook (placeholder link)
Samir: Added SLO dashboards and threshold alerts to the ticket.
Jonah K: Canary 2% started at 1846240000. Will report p50/p95 in ~2 hours.
Alex W: Closing thread until metrics in. Great work finding a middle path. :thumbsup:
